title: Check yourself: Chunks, BM25 and embeddings

questions.stem: A support bot must find the passage that contains the error code E-4012. Which approach is the reliable one?

options.text: Only a reranker, since the earlier stages cannot see digits
options.says: Ruled out because the reranker is the optional fifth stage, and the page says the keyword index "finds `E-4012` when the query holds it".

options.text: An embedding of every passage, because a code has a meaning like other codes
options.says: Ruled out because an embedding "is weaker with exact strings".

options.text: Neither, because a code is too short to be indexed at all
options.says: Ruled out because "A rare word such as an error code outweighs common words".

options.text: A keyword index, because it matches the exact term as written
options.says: The page says "BM25 is exact. It finds `E-4012` when the query holds it."

questions.stem: A team asks where to get embeddings for Claude-based retrieval. What does the documentation say?

options.text: Anthropic has no model of its own, and names Voyage AI as a provider
options.says: The page quotes "Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model." and names Voyage AI.

options.text: Use the embedding endpoint of the Messages API, which every model has
options.says: Ruled out because "Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model", so no endpoint exists.

options.text: Ask Claude to write the vectors, since it understands the text
options.says: Ruled out because an embedding model is a trained model that "turns text into a vector of numbers", not a text generator.

options.text: Train a model on the Claude API's logs, which are provided for this
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation tells you to "assess a variety of embeddings vendors", and says nothing about logs.

questions.stem: A cut falls in the middle of a key sentence of three words, and the overlap is four words. What does overlap do about it?

options.text: The sentence is stored twice, as a single longer chunk of its own
options.says: Ruled out because each window "repeats the last `overlap` words of the one before it", and does not build a separate chunk.

options.text: The sentence is dropped from every chunk so that no half survives
options.says: Ruled out because "a sentence cut at a boundary loses its meaning on both sides", and overlap keeps it.

options.text: At least one window keeps it intact, as the repeated span is longer
options.says: The page says "with an overlap at least as long as the sentence, at least one chunk holds it whole".

options.text: The cut moves to the next paragraph without being asked
options.says: Ruled out because windows are cut by words: "the last window ends at the last word".
